item.title: SoftBank Names Ex-Goldman Sachs Trader Agne to Lead Vision Fund Finances
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. has picked former Goldman Sachs trader Mark Agne to oversee finance and technology at the Vision Fund, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Vanguard Buys Inflation-Protected Bonds on an Oil-Market Oddity
item.description: Unusual moves in an oil-market gauge are prompting Vanguard Asset Management Ltd. to buy insurance against stickier-than-expected US inflation.

item.title: India Power Giant Seeks Uranium Assets Overseas in Nuclear Push
item.description: India’s largest power producer is seeking to invest in overseas uranium mines to secure supplies needed to fuel 30 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity it plans to build over the next two decades.

item.title: EU Banks Urged to Pool Buying Power in Deals With US Tech Giants
item.description: Banks and finance firms should combine their buying power to avoid losing out in negotiations with US tech giants, according to raft of Dutch proposals aimed at tackling Europe’s over-dependence on foreign providers of critical services such as AI and cloud computing.

item.title: South Africa Economy Nears ‘Escape Velocity,’ Standard Bank Says
item.description: South African economic growth is on an upswing as the nation chips away at the bottlenecks that have held it back for years, said Standard Bank Group Ltd.

item.title: Tycoon Dewji Expands Into Battery Minerals as Demand Surges
item.description: Tanzanian tycoon Mohammed Dewji is investing in graphite mining and luxury tourism to help his MeTL Group benefit from the global scramble for minerals needed for electric-vehicle batteries and Africa’s booming high-end travel market.

item.title: Bayer Sells $3.4 Billion Contraceptives Stake to Apollo
item.description: Bayer AG sold a minority stake in its contraceptives business to Apollo Global Management Inc. for €3 billion ($3.4 billion) and will use the funds raised to help cover its ballooning litigation costs tied to the herbicide Roundup.

item.title: EasyJet Gets £5.7 Billion Apollo Bid Gatecrashing Castlelake
item.description: EasyJet Plc received a fresh offer from private equity firm Apollo Global Management for 715 pence a share that beats a rival proposal from Castlelake LP, a surprise twist in the takeover saga that sets up a possible bidding war between the two US investment funds.

item.title: FTSE 100 Outperforms European Tech Weakness
SK Hynix’s US Trading Debut Unleashes Wave of New Leveraged ETFs
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s record-setting US debut is paving the way for a fresh wave of leveraged products tied to the South Korean memory giant’s shares, bringing to Wall Street the popular bets that have amplified the stock’s volatility in Seoul.

item.title: Niel Becomes Biggest Vodafone Investor With $6 Billion Deal
item.description: French billionaire Xavier Niel has agreed to buy a stake in Vodafone Group Plc from Emirates Telecommunications Group Co. for about $6 billion to become the biggest shareholder in the British telecommunications company.

item.title: SocGen to Finance Tycoon’s Cameroon Sugar Mill to Take on Castel
item.description: Societe Generale SA is arranging a syndicated loan for Cameroonian tycoon Nassourou Issa to finance a sugar mill that will rival a facility controlled by the billionaire Castel family.

item.title: Technoprobe’s 330% Surge Makes It a European AI Stock Standout
item.description: An Italian firm whose products are key to the chips being made by Nvidia Corp. has emerged as one of Europe’s biggest winners in the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Carry Trades Face Best Conditions Since 2000, Goldman Says
item.description: Carry trades — one of the most widely-used strategies in the $9.5 trillion-per-day currency market — are seeing the most compelling backdrop in more than two decades, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

item.title: China Omits Job Goal in Five-Year Plan for First Time in Decades
item.description: China set no numeric target for urban job creation for the first time in at least three decades, in an apparent nod to rising uncertainty over employment as AI spreads through the economy.

item.title: Yen Traders Ask How Japan Pension Money Can Sustain Rally
item.description: The big question for traders tracking the yen’s sudden rally on Friday is whether the government will follow through on its call to draw the country’s huge pension chest back into investments at home.

item.title: Corn Steadies Ahead of Key US Supply Report as Heat Threats Ease
item.description: Corn futures steadied ahead of a key monthly US report on supply and demand, while concerns about weather risks eased.

item.title: AI Could Affect Millions in Asean as ILO Sees No Big Job Cuts
item.description: Artificial intelligence could reshape the jobs of nearly 80 million people across Southeast Asia, but there is little sign it has led to large-scale employment cuts, according to the International Labour Organization.

item.title: A Hidden-Debt Scandal Derails Senegal's Infrastructure Dream
item.description: Unfinished railway is emblematic of the country’s fiscal strains.

item.title: Payment Firms Emerge as Target in Fight Against Illegal Casinos In Lithuania
item.description: A trade body for European gambling companies has filed a complaint to the Lithuanian banking regulator seeking an investigation of a payment company that it alleges props up illegal online casinos.

item.title: Adani Flagship Is the Next Big India Pick for Singapore’s Helios
item.description: Helios Capital Management is betting on the flagship stock of India’s Adani Group to be the next big winner for its funds in a market left behind in the global AI frenzy.

item.title: Malaysia’s Anwar to Debut an AI Double That Sounds Just Like Him
item.description: Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is about to do something very few heads of government have done: send an artificial intelligence version of himself out to meet the public.

item.title: Tencent in Talks to Become Manus’ Largest Holder, FT Reports
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd. is in discussions to become the largest shareholder in Manus, the Chinese agentic AI pioneer whose blockbuster acquisition by Meta Platforms Inc. was struck down by Beijing, the Financial Times reported.

item.title: Iron Ore Set For Weekly Gain on BHP Port Strike, FMG Stalemate
item.description: Iron ore was on track for the biggest weekly gain since early May as a looming strike at BHP Group’s Port Hedland terminal stoked supply concerns, even as fundamentals remain tested.

item.title: Rupee May be Tested as RBI Unwinds Bearish Dollar Bets
item.description: Short dollar forward positions ballooned to $106.7 billion in May.

item.title: Modi Visit Showcases New Zealand Leader Luxon’s Trade Coup Ahead of Tight Ballot
item.description: Narendra Modi’s visit to Auckland — the first by an Indian prime minister in four decades — highlights one of New Zealand leader Christopher Luxon’s biggest foreign policy coups: securing a free trade agreement with the world’s most populous nation.

item.title: Strategists Diverge on Long-Term Yen Trend After Katayama Speech
item.description: Some strategists see a boost to assets, while others were sceptical of a sustained rally, following Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama’s comments Friday encouraging pension funds, including the massive Government Pension Investment Fund, to increase investment in domestic financial assets. Here’s what strategists are saying:

item.title: Copper Heads for Weekly Gain as Traders Look Past Iran Flare-Up
item.description: Copper was on track for its second straight weekly gain as investors looked past potential demand headwinds presented by the mid-week resurgence in fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Japan’s Long Bonds, Yen Rise on Push for More GPIF Investment
item.description: Japan’s long-term bond yields fell and the yen strengthened after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said the government wants to encourage pension funds, including the Government Pension Investment Fund, to increase investment in domestic financial assets.

item.title: AI, Iran War Risks Weigh on Indian IT Firms’ Earnings Outlook
item.description: HCL Technologies Ltd., Wipro Ltd. and Tech Mahindra Ltd. are set to report earnings as their investor base increasingly questions the value of traditional IT services in the age of artificial intelligence.
